cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Heavily backward-integrated manufacture. 'We are among the very few companies in the world with a backward-integrated manufacturing facility for thermocouples, cables, and electrical heaters, located at Udaipur, India, as of March 31, 2026 (Source: F&S Report).' Key in-house capabilities now include alloy melting, hot-rolling, annealing, mineral-insulated cable manufacturing, machining, final assembly and calibration: 'Previously, we relied on external suppliers for most metallurgical finished goods, but by internalising these critical steps, we have reduced our dependence on third parties.' For heater products the Company manufactures heating alloys, produces tubular heating elements, fabricates vessels and performs final assembly including instrumentation, process connections and panel integration entirely in-house, and also produces the thermocouple conductor used in thermocouple cables - stated to have 'increased operational control, enhanced product consistency, and allowed us to shorten lead times'. Certain units manufacture products used as raw materials by other units as well as being supplied to external customers. New products are frequently used internally before external launch (thermowells, thermocouple cables, mineral-insulated and specialised cables, thermocouple and heating-alloy nickel-based conductors). Indigenisation is framed under 'Make in India': thermocouple and heating conductors previously imported are now manufactured in-house, and the Company states it has 'reduced reliance on foreign suppliers' by indigenising non-contact temperature sensor development. Manufacturing is make-to-order: 'Each manufacturing job operates on a make-to-order basis, i.e., customer requirements are translated into detailed engineering and design workflows, resulting in precise production drawings.' INPUTS: metals and alloys (platinum, nickel, stainless steel, copper, inconel), insulating materials (magnesium oxide, ceramics, fibreglass, PTFE), coatings (silicone, PVC, polyimide). Cost of materials procured from India was Rs 2,095.61 / 1,681.12 / 1,419.40 million and from outside India Rs 512.04 / 408.29 / 235.76 million for Fiscals 2026 / 2025 / 2024, i.e. 80.36% / 80.46% / 85.76% domestic and 19.64% / 19.54% / 14.24% imported; purchases during the year were Rs 2,607.65 / 2,089.41 / 1,655.16 million (71.63% / 69.12% / 72.88% of total expenses) and cost of materials consumed Rs 2,484.25 / 1,985.13 / 1,717.06 million (68.24% / 65.67% / 75.60% of total expenses). Suppliers span 18 Indian states and two union territories and 18 foreign countries (including China, USA, UK, Singapore, Germany, Israel, France, Austria, Czech Republic, Japan, South Korea, Indonesia, UAE, Thailand, Canada, Taiwan and Hong Kong). FORWARD/OUTBOUND: no owned logistics - 'We rely on third-party logistics providers ... We do not operate our own logistics fleet, nor do we conduct logistics operations through related party transactions. We rely on spot-based arrangements with third-party logistics providers, utilising air, road, and rail transportation modes.' R&D is conducted entirely in-house with a dedicated team of 83 employees as of March 31, 2026 (10.20% of total group headcount of 814); granted IP comprises 12 patents in India, eight registered trademarks in India, one copyright registration in India and 39 trademark registrations outside India, with one patent, four Indian trademarks and three foreign trademarks pending. Working capital: Net Working Capital Days of 210 / 193 / 152 for Fiscals 2026 / 2025 / 2024 (days sales outstanding plus days inventory outstanding minus days payable outstanding), the increase 'primarily attributable to a higher inventory holding resulting from customization requirements, delays in dispatch clearance, and the impact of the amalgamation of Marathon Heater ... acquisition of Tempsens GmbH, Tempsens Polaska and Tempsens Measurement and Control Private Limited'.

demand_drivers.body: Affirmative nil. Segment reporting: 'There is only one reportable segment, i.e., industrial products.'

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Our Projects/OEM business principally involve large, sometimes one-time, orders as part of new installations or major upgrades at customers’ facilities.
- In contrast, our MRO business involves supplying regular replacement parts, such as cables and sensors, to both existing Projects/OEM customers and new accounts.
- While the MRO business promotes recurring revenue and helps support ongoing customer relationships, there is a risk that the smaller and more frequent nature of these orders may limit our ability to generate substantial revenue growth or offset fluctuations in larger Projects/OEM transactions.
- The Project/OEM business category is sensitive to economic downturns or reductions in customer capital expenditure; delays or cancellations of major projects can suppress growth.
- In the MRO business, lower demand may arise if customers extend lifecycles of their thermal components, implement efficiency improvements, or shift to alternative products or suppliers.
- While we have not witnessed any significant reduction in demand for our products from customers both in Projects/OEM and MRO business categories during Fiscals 2026, 2025, and 2024, we cannot assure you that the reduction in demand from such customers will not happen going forward.
- A sustained decline, disruption or loss of business in either business category could lower our operational leverage and reduce the predictability of our revenue.
- Although our customer base is diversified across multiple end-user industries, our revenue remains exposed to demand fluctuations within certain key sectors.
